benefits.name: Disabled Veterans Homestead Deduction
benefits.description: The District of Columbia reduces the assessed value of a disabled veteran's home by $445,000 for property tax purposes. To qualify, the veteran must be classified by the VA with a total permanent disability from a service-incurred or service-aggravated condition, or be rated at 100% disability for individual unemployability; occupy the property (of no more than five dwelling units) as their principal residence; hold at least 50% ownership per deed; be domiciled in the District; and have total household federal adjusted gross income not exceeding $163,500 (tax year 2026). The property cannot be held in an irrevocable trust (except a special needs trust) and cannot be owned by a corporation or LLC. Recipients cannot simultaneously claim the Homestead Deduction, Senior Citizen/Disabled Tax Relief, or the tax cap credit. Effective October 1, 2022.

otherReqs: Property occupied as principal residence, no more than 5 dwelling units
Domiciled in the District of Columbia
Total household federal AGI not exceeding $163,500 (TY2026)
Property not held in irrevocable trust (except special needs trust) or owned by a corporation/LLC
Cannot be combined with Homestead Deduction, Senior Citizen/Disabled Tax Relief, or tax cap credit

application.agency: DC Office of Tax and Revenue / Mayor's Office of Veterans Affairs
documentation: VA determination of total permanent disability or 100% individual unemployability rating

benefits.name: Disabled American Veteran (DAV) License Tags
benefits.description: DC veterans with a service-connected permanent and total disability, as documented by a VA letter indicating 'Total and Permanent' status, may receive one set of tags (DAV, Veteran, or passenger) at no fee for a non-commercial vehicle. The fee waiver applies only to the annual registration fee, not to other DMV fees. To obtain a Disabled American Veteran tag with the DAV symbol specifically, the applicant must also hold certified membership with the District of Columbia Disabled American Veterans organization, verified by the Commander, in addition to the VA authorization letter and an approved DC DMV Disability Tag/Placard application.
benefits.value: One set of tags issued at no fee for a non-commercial vehicle (annual registration fee only)

otherReqs: DAV-symbol tag additionally requires certified DC DAV organization membership verified by the Commander

documentation: VA authorization letter documenting 'Total and Permanent' service-connected disability
Approved DC DMV Disability Tag/Placard application

benefits.name: DC Government Veterans' Preference
benefits.description: The District of Columbia government grants veterans' preference during the competitive hiring process to disabled veterans, veterans who served on active duty during certain time periods or military operations, and, under certain conditions, to eligible spouses, widows, widowers, or mothers of deceased or disabled veterans. Applicants for positions in the Legal, Executive, Excepted, and Management Supervisory Service are not eligible for veterans' preference. Applicants who retired at or above the rank of Major or Lieutenant Commander are not eligible unless the retirement is based on a service-connected disability. This session could not confirm specific point values against a directly-read official source; DCHR directs applicants to Chapter 7A of the DC personnel regulations for full detail.
benefits.value: Hiring preference during the competitive selection process for eligible veterans and disabled veterans

otherReqs: Not applicable to Legal, Executive, Excepted, or Management Supervisory Service positions
Retirees at or above Major/Lieutenant Commander rank ineligible unless retirement was for a service-connected disability
Official proof of veteran status must be submitted with the application

documentation: DD-214 or other official proof of veteran status

benefits.name: UDC Veteran In-State Tuition
benefits.description: The University of the District of Columbia grants veterans the resident (in-state) tuition rate upon proof of military status, such as active-duty military orders or discharge papers, waiving the standard 90-day residency requirement for qualifying active-duty and recently discharged service members and their dependents. Veterans seeking to use VA education benefits at UDC must also complete the UDC VA Education Enrollment Form; not all programs (e.g., Ed2Go certificate programs) are approved for VA educational benefits.
benefits.value: In-state (resident) tuition rate at UDC for qualifying veterans, waiving the standard 90-day residency requirement

otherReqs: Proof of military status (active duty orders or discharge papers) required
UDC VA Education Enrollment Form required to use VA educational benefits
Not all UDC programs are VA-benefit-approved

application.agency: University of the District of Columbia, Office of Military and Veteran Student Services
documentation: Military orders or discharge papers proving military/veteran status
